On Windows CI, "a tracked local file of another letter case never infers local" found local because git add of a case variant on NTFS added nothing, and "a tracked top-level entry that is the .claude folder by identity never infers local" failed because writing .claude. lands in .claude. The fix adds index entries with git hash-object and update-index --cacheinfo and asserts the index holds them.

Check: each test still asserts user scope and would fail if the product check regressed; the new index assertions prevent a vacuous pass; nothing in the setup is invalid on Windows (path separators, NTFS name rules, core.protectNTFS on update-index).

**result:** No coverage lost and no vacuous pass found. Both rebuilt setups are valid on Windows, with one unverified residual. I ran the file on Linux only.

**findings:**
**Case-variant test** (`packages/runtime/tests/setup-scope.test.ts:796-818`): it still asserts the full setup output.
  - `lines[0]` must be `DEFAULT` (user scope), and `lines[1]` must be the "git tracks it" notice naming `target.local`.
  - If the product's tracked-case check regressed, the local file would infer local and `lines[0]` would differ.
  - The new `icase,literal` pathspec assertion at lines 806-808 requires the index to hold `.claude/Settings.Local.json`. If the setup tracked nothing, the test now fails in setup instead of passing vacuously. The existing literal-name assertion at lines 803-805 still shows the literal name is untracked.
**`.claude.` identity test** (`:836-874`): it still asserts the full setup output, including the `.claude. as .claude` notice at line 869.
  - The new assertion at lines 843-845 requires the index to hold exactly `.claude./settings.local.json`.
  - The local file at `.claude/settings.local.json` is no longer overwritten on Windows, so the "enabled" local file the test relies on survives.
  - The `lstat` spy is unchanged and still folds `.claude.` onto `.claude`.
**`trackEntry`** (`:576-582`): it works on Linux and all 66 tests pass.

**Windows validity:**
`blob.json` is built with `join(home, …)` and passed as a native path, so there are no separator problems.
The cacheinfo path argument uses forward slashes, which is what git expects.
`core.protectNTFS` rejects `.git` look-alikes and backslashes. `.claude.` and `Settings.Local.json` are neither, so `update-index --add --cacheinfo` should accept them.
No `.claude.` is created on disk any more, which was the actual Windows failure.
**Residual, not run:** Windows runs with `core.ignorecase=true`, which I could not check. A pathspec without `icase` might match case-insensitively there. I read pathspec matching as magic-flag-driven, so the literal-name emptiness assertion at lines 803-805 should hold. That assertion was already in the test before this commit.

**verdict:** Approve; the Windows CI run is the only remaining confirmation.
